spans.s:
Vapa, ‘sower,’ is mentioned in the list of victims at the Puruṣamedha (‘human sacrifice’) in the yajurveda.
Foot notes Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xxx. 7; taittirīya brāhmaṇa, iii. 4, 3, 1.

Vapā in the later Saṃhitās and the Brāhmaṇas denotes an ant-hill.
Foot notes taittirīya Saṃhitā, v. 1, 2, 5; taittirīya brāhmaṇa, i. 1, 3, 4; Satapatha brāhmaṇa, vi. 3, 3, 5.

Vapana in the Brāhmaṇas denotes the process of ‘shaving.’ Cf. kṣura and keśa.
Foot notes taittirīya Saṃhitā, ii. 7, 17, 1; Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, iii. 1, 2, 1.

Vaptṛ in the Rigveda and later denotes a ‘shaver,’ ‘barber.’
Foot notes x. 142, 4.
Av. viii. 2, 17; taittirīya brāhmaṇa, i. 5, 6, 3.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 266; Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East, 32, 235, n. 4.

Vapra, ‘rampart,’ is a conjectural reading in the Atharvaveda.
Foot notes vii. 71, 1. See Whitney, Translation of the Atharvaveda, 435, 436.
